name: Left Ventricular Non-Compaction Cardiomyopathy Pediatric Form

criteria.description: Prominent trabeculations with a non-compacted to compacted myocardium ratio >2:1 at end-systole on echocardiography
Presence of deep intertrabecular recesses perfused from the ventricular cavity demonstrated by color Doppler
Left ventricular systolic dysfunction or heart failure symptoms in a pediatric patient
Exclusion of other causes of cardiomyopathy such as dilated or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of prominent trabeculations with non-compacted to compacted ratio >2:1 and deep intertrabecular recesses on imaging, plus exclusion of other cardiomyopathies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Cardiac MRI may be used to confirm diagnosis when echocardiographic findings are inconclusive.

pathognomonic.notes: Visualized on echocardiography or cardiac MRI

pathognomonic.symptomName: Deep intertrabecular recesses with blood flow
searchTerms: deep heart muscle recesses with blood flow

common.notes: Due to left ventricular systolic dysfunction
searchTerms: symptoms of heart failure like breathlessness
fatigue and shortness of breath from heart problems

common.notes: Includes atrial fibrillation and ventricular tachycardia
searchTerms: abnormal heart rhythms from ventricles or atria

common.notes: May be due to ischemia or arrhythmia

occasional.notes: Due to stagnant blood flow in recesses

rare.notes: Due to right heart failure in advanced disease

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) or NT-proBNP in heart failure
Possible elevated troponin in myocardial injury
imaging: Echocardiography showing prominent trabeculations and non-compacted to compacted myocardium ratio >2:1
Cardiac MRI confirming trabeculations and recesses with delayed gadolinium enhancement
Color Doppler demonstrating blood flow within recesses
genetic: Mutations in sarcomeric genes such as MYH7, ACTC1, and others associated with familial LVNC
other: Electrocardiogram abnormalities including ventricular arrhythmias, conduction delays

redFlags: Sudden onset of syncope or presyncope
Ventricular tachyarrhythmias on ECG or Holter
Rapid progression of heart failure symptoms
references: Jenni R, et al. Echocardiographic and pathoanatomical characteristics of isolated left ventricular non-compaction: a step towards classification as a distinct cardiomyopathy. Heart. 2001.
Towbin JA, et al. Left ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy. Lancet. 2015.
Oechslin EN, et al. Left ventricular noncompaction: a distinct cardiomyopathy? J Am Coll Cardiol. 2000.
